feature.title: 対局操作の再試行・永続化・復旧

source.needle: async fn apply(&mut self, pending: MutationRequest) -> Result<Acceptance, ApplicationError> {

flow: The per-game actor refreshes durable history and checks participant membership, exact accepted request replay, then expected sequence before staging a cloned legal candidate.
StagedGameChange freezes the acceptance and canonical event batch; commit_change performs version comparison and persists metadata, one receipt and those events atomically.

After an uncertain/conflicting commit the actor reloads durable receipts, returns the original acceptance when present and otherwise reports conflict/unavailability while fencing uncertain local state.
Caller cancellation after enqueue leaves the actor transaction running; restart reconstructs receipts, and dropping the final service sender lets queued commands drain.

guarantees.statement: Only acceptance reserves a per-game request identity. After participant checks, an exact typed action/user/original expected-sequence retry returns the original acceptance before stale/finished checks, even after restart; changed accepted content conflicts.
Each new committed command advances sequence once through i64::MAX. Per-game actor processing and repository CAS serialize competing service instances and refresh losing state.

Candidate position becomes visible only after confirmed commit. Metadata, receipt and supplied canonical events commit together: move emits MoveCommitted, mate appends GameFinished at the same sequence, resignation emits GameFinished. Replay/rejection/restore emit nothing new.

An error may follow a durable commit. The actor reconciles a matching stored receipt or invalidates its state until a later successful durable refresh; failed reads never authorize continued cached mutation.
The 64-slot per-game mailbox bounds queued commands. Cancellation after enqueue does not undo execution; cancellation before enqueue does not execute, and closed senders allow queued work to drain.

contracts.statement: Replay first checks participant membership then compares the complete MutationRequest under the game-scoped accepted ID and returns its original Acceptance.

evidence.reason: Exact move/resign retries after finish return original acceptances; changed sequence/user/move/action conflict with no extra advance.
Original receipts survive ongoing and finished state across two server restarts.
Same request identity in separate games/services remains independent.
Every tested rejection preserves full snapshot and leaves the request ID reusable.

contracts.statement: Mutation refreshes state, applies replay before expected sequence checks, stages a cloned candidate and supplied events, and publishes in-memory candidate only after commit confirmation.

source.needle: async fn apply(&mut self, pending: MutationRequest) -> Result<Acceptance, ApplicationError> {

evidence.reason: Fake repository observes exact staged move/resignation events before commit and only two writes despite replay/rejection.
Synthetic actor cases assert request-conflict before sequence mismatch before finished-game rejection.
Independent real store/service instances serialize CAS conflicts and identical concurrent retries.
Commit-after-error reconciles receipt; precommit failure fences until durable reads recover.

contracts.statement: next_sequence rejects advancing i64::MAX; stale expected sequence is checked before attempting an exhausted advance.

evidence.reason: Direct helper asserts portable maximum and exhausted boundary.
Synthetic exhausted actor distinguishes stale SequenceMismatch from SequenceExhausted.

contracts.gap: Tests synthesize maximum state; they do not prove the rules engine supports billions of actual moves.

contracts.statement: PostgreSQL commit_change compares expected version and atomically saves metadata, receipt, frozen supplied events and terminal dependent records; no partial success is exposed.

source.needle: async fn commit_change(&self, change: &StagedGameChange) -> Result<(), Error> {

evidence.reason: Independent service/store instances CAS and refresh correctly.
Injected actual statement/commit errors leave both metadata and receipt unchanged.
Outbox enqueue failure rolls back game metadata, journal and events.
Missing both terminal ticket records prevents result/receipt/outbox/job writes together.

contracts.statement: StagedGameChange validates sequence bounds/continuity and action/result combinations, then freezes normal move, move-plus-checkmate or resignation event order.

source.needle: pub fn new(game_id: GameId, receipt: Receipt) -> Result<Self, ApplicationError> {

evidence.reason: Exact normal move, same-sequence move-then-mate-finish and resignation batches are compared; inconsistent action/result cases reject.
Zero/noncontiguous/max/out-of-range acceptance and expected sequence boundaries are checked.
Persisted event payload stays frozen; retry/rejection/restoration add no duplicate events.

contracts.statement: Reload clears local state before reading/validating durable history; failed reconciliation leaves it unavailable until a later refresh can restore it.

source.needle: async fn reload(&mut self) -> Result<(), ApplicationError> {

evidence.reason: Fault adapter around real PostgreSQL tests commit-after-error receipt recovery, precommit failure, unreadable fencing and later recovery.

contracts.gap: The fault adapter controls representative outcome paths; arbitrary process/crash interleavings are not proven.

contracts.statement: The per-game facade uses a 64-command bounded channel; actor execution outlives dropped reply receivers and drains closed queues.

evidence.reason: Dropped response and closed mailbox still execute queued commands.
A capacity-blocked cancelled send does not execute while an enqueued cancelled call does.
Closed actor reloads durable store and final service drop closes senders.

contracts.gap: 64 bounds queued slots, excluding in-progress work and waiting senders. No global known-game actor registry bound or fairness guarantee is established.

limitations: Successful representative fault/concurrency tests do not prove all crash schedules or durable infrastructure guarantees.
Game command trace owns canonical event production and atomic enqueue; publication, subscriber delivery and rating application are separate feature records.
Actor/mailbox fairness, total memory for known-game registries and an upper bound on waiting callers are not promised.
Links and passing tests do not establish semantic completeness; changes to guarantees, evidence strength and decomposition require review.
